value.rationale: The 2026 motivating theory makes the operator-extension property a central criterion but does not provide its modulus. The zero-sum plane of a real three-dimensional cube is the smallest ambient dimension in which Hilbert-valued operator extension is nontrivial (scalar one-dimensional domain is covered by Hahn–Banach). This gives a sharp uniform n-independent quantitative constant, an explicit optimal-extension construction, and rigidity of every extremizing map. The \(2/\sqrt3\) factor is strictly less than the elementary \(4/3\) mean-zero projection norm and is not a mere relabeling of Euclidean Banach–Mazur distance. It provides a reusable exact model for quantitative POE-2 research, without claiming a general downstream theorem.
